title: ⭐ Practice: putting the small words in place

questions.prompt: Complete: "The two cooks arrived at six. ___ prepared the bread before the shop opened."
questions.explanation: "They" is right: a subject pronoun stands before the verb and does the action — They prepared the bread. "Them" is the object form and belongs after a verb or a preposition, "Their" is a possessive adjective and needs a noun straight after it, and "He" would point at one man while the sentence names two cooks.

questions.prompt: Complete: "Karim forgot his knives, so the chef lent a set to ___ before service."
questions.explanation: "him" is right: after a preposition the object form is compulsory, so to is followed by him. "he" is the subject form and can never follow to, "his" is a possessive adjective and needs a noun straight after it, and "them" would point at several people while the sentence names one cook, Karim.

questions.prompt: Complete: "Amira phoned ___ father to say that the exam had gone well."
questions.explanation: "her" is right: a possessive adjective follows the owner, and the owner here is Amira, a woman — Amira phoned her father. "his" makes the possessive agree with father, the person owned, which English never does; "she" is a subject pronoun and cannot stand in front of a noun; and "their" would need several owners.

questions.prompt: Read this passage: "Hela left school at seventeen and opened a small bakery with her sister. Their parents were worried, because the loan was large and the two girls were very young. 'We will pay it back in three years,' Hela promised them. Today the bakery employs six people, and its bread is sold in every shop in the town." Who does "We" point at in Hela's promise?
questions.explanation: "Hela and her sister" is right: We is a subject pronoun, and Hela is the one speaking — she answers for herself and for the sister she opened the bakery with, since the loan is the two girls' loan. "Hela's parents" and "Hela and her parents" both put the parents inside the promise, although the parents are the people the promise is made to: Hela promised them. "the people of the town" only appear at the end, where the bread is sold.

questions.prompt: Rewrite this sentence with pronouns: "Faten met Slim in Faten's restaurant."

options.text: Her met him in her restaurant.
She met him in her restaurant.
She met him in his restaurant.
She met him in Faten's restaurant.

questions.explanation: "She met him in her restaurant." is right: Faten becomes she before the verb, Slim becomes him after it, and Faten's becomes the possessive her in front of restaurant. "Her met him in her restaurant." puts an object form where the subject belongs; "She met him in his restaurant." gives the restaurant to Slim although it belongs to Faten; and "She met him in Faten's restaurant." leaves the name in place instead of replacing it.

questions.prompt: Complete: "The restaurant closed last year because ___ owner moved abroad."
questions.explanation: "its" is right: the possessive adjective of it carries no apostrophe and stands immediately before a noun — its owner. "it's" is the short form of it is, which cannot stand in front of owner; "his" would turn the restaurant into a man; and "their" would need several owners.
